title: A copy record and a perfectly good 1:1 match, disagreeing
why: The conflict the dominance table exists for, made mechanical. occ-b1 really does satisfy R-CONT-SAME-SITE - same file, same symbol, same content - so a mapper reading one edge at a time reaches `continued` honestly and drops occ-b2 on the floor. R-BRANCH-COPY reads the successor SET and the record that explains it. Both fire; the case pins that both must be RECORDED as firing and that the branch reading wins. A fixture that showed only the right outcome would pass while dominance did no work at all.

expect.note: R-CONT-SAME-SITE stays in applicable_rules and out of licensed_by. It proposed `continued` to occ-b1 and lost; recording it as licensing `branched` would attribute a conclusion to a rule that never reached it, and dropping it would lose the recall set - retiring R-BRANCH-COPY later must find exactly this mapping.
